profile.reading: This is The Rock, an underground data center at Kivipellontie 35b in Ulvila, near Pori on Finlands west coast, built inside a set of nine ex-military bedrock tunnels originally quarried by the Finnish Defense Forces in the 1960s and repurposed into a data center when Ficolo acquired the tunnels in 2011. The nine tunnel halls, ranging from about 500 to 800 square meters each, together total roughly 8,500 square meters, and the naturally cool bedrock holds an average temperature of about 8 degrees Celsius, reducing active cooling needs even as the facility has begun transitioning from traditional air cooling to direct liquid cooling using Dell DLC3000 units delivering up to 80 kilowatts of cooling capacity each, a shift expected to cut cooling energy use from about 20 percent to 10 percent of total IT power draw. The site runs on renewable power from nearby wind farms and an on site 2,600 square meter solar installation, with total facility capacity reported at around 10 to 11 megawatts once fully built out. Later operated by Verne (formerly Verne Global), The Rock was sold along with the smaller Deck facility in Tampere to Nordic cloud infrastructure provider Glesys in a deal announced October 14, 2025 on undisclosed terms, as Verne redirected its own investment toward a planned 70 megawatt facility in Mantsala and expansion of its Helsinki campus. Before the Glesys sale, Ficolo Oy had operated three Finnish sites, Helsinki (the Air), this Pori facility (the Rock), and Tampere (the Deck), all powered by 100 percent sustainable energy, and began operating under the Verne Global brand starting October 18, 2022, when the two companies combined to form a broader Nordic data center platform with about 23 megawatts of available capacity and potential to expand to 90 megawatts across the three Finnish sites. Both Verne Global and Ficolo were, at the time of that combination, part of Triple Points Digital 9 Infrastructure plc portfolio, and Verne separately operates a renewable powered campus in Iceland that was expected to reach 40 megawatts of constructed capacity in 2023, plus a data center hub in London.
